title: Substances and mixtures - 123 school
heading: Substances and mixtures
intro: Test your knowledge by typing your answer and comparing it with the correct answer. Then click 'Check answers'.

questions.q: Name three properties of a substance
questions.a: For example: colour, smell, taste, state, melting point, boiling point, density

questions.q: What is a safety data sheet (chemical data card)?
questions.a: A sheet with information about the properties of a substance, including the hazardous ones

questions.q: Name two hazard symbols
questions.a: For example: flammable, harmful, explosive, corrosive, toxic

questions.q: What is the melting point?
questions.a: The temperature at which a substance melts. The freezing point is the same.

questions.q: What is the boiling point?
questions.a: The temperature at which a substance boils

questions.q: What are the melting point and the boiling point of water?
questions.a: Melting point 0 °C and boiling point 100 °C

questions.q: What is the boiling point of ethanol (alcohol) in kelvin? (use BINAS table 16)
questions.a: 351 K (that is 78 °C)

questions.q: Give the formula for density
questions.a: density = mass / volume (ρ = m / V)

questions.q: Which unit goes with density?
questions.a: g/cm<sup>3</sup>

questions.q: A substance has a mass of 60 g and a volume of 20 cm<sup>3</sup>. What is its density?
questions.a: 60 g ÷ 20 cm<sup>3</sup> = 3 g/cm<sup>3</sup>

questions.q: What is the density of aluminium? (use BINAS table 15)
questions.a: 2.70 g/cm<sup>3</sup>

questions.q: Does a block of copper float on water? Look up the densities. (use BINAS tables 15 and 16)
questions.a: No. Copper has a density of 8.96 g/cm<sup>3</sup> and water 1.00 g/cm<sup>3</sup>. The density of copper is greater, so copper sinks.

questions.q: Wood has a density of 0.6 g/cm<sup>3</sup> and water has a density of 1.0 g/cm<sup>3</sup>. Does the wood float on water?
questions.a: Yes, the density of wood is lower than that of water

questions.q: Name the four state symbols
questions.a: (s) solid, (l) liquid, (g) gas and (aq) dissolved in water (aqueous)

questions.q: Name the six changes of state
questions.a: Melting, freezing, evaporating, condensing, sublimation and deposition

questions.q: What is the name of the change of state from solid to gas?
questions.a: Sublimation

questions.q: What is the name of the change of state from gas to solid?
questions.a: Deposition

questions.q: Is a change of state a chemical reaction?
questions.a: No, the molecules do not change

questions.q: What happens to the molecules when you heat a substance?
questions.a: They move faster

questions.q: How are the molecules arranged in a solid?
questions.a: Close together in fixed positions. They vibrate.

questions.q: What is a pure substance?
questions.a: A substance that consists of one type of molecule

questions.q: What is a mixture?
questions.a: A substance that consists of several types of molecules

questions.q: Name two pure substances
questions.a: For example: ethanol, acetone, diamond, sugar crystals, washing soda, distilled water

questions.q: Name two mixtures
questions.a: For example: air, tap water, cola, paint, cement, coffee

questions.q: What happens to the temperature when a pure substance melts?
questions.a: The temperature stays the same

questions.q: What happens to the temperature when a mixture melts?
questions.a: The temperature changes. The interval is called the melting range (for freezing or boiling: freezing range or boiling range).

questions.q: What is a solution?
questions.a: A clear, sometimes coloured liquid in which one or more substances have dissolved

questions.q: What is a solvent?
questions.a: The liquid in which you dissolve a substance. For example water.

questions.q: What is a suspension?
questions.a: A cloudy mixture of solid particles in a liquid. Paint is an example.

questions.q: What is an emulsion?
questions.a: A cloudy mixture of two liquids that do not mix, with small droplets

questions.q: What is an emulsifier?
questions.a: A substance that holds an emulsion together. For example soap or egg yolk.

questions.q: What happens in a chemical reaction?
questions.a: The reactants disappear and new substances form (the products)

questions.q: Where are the reactants in a reaction scheme?
questions.a: Before the arrow

questions.q: Give the reaction scheme for the burning of magnesium
questions.a: magnesium (s) + oxygen (g) → magnesium oxide (s)

questions.q: What do you use acetone, petroleum ether and methylated spirits for as solvents?
questions.a: Acetone: nail polish. Petroleum ether and methylated spirits: grease.

questions.q: Name the three types of Bunsen burner flame and what you use each for
questions.a: Yellow flame (safety flame, when you are not heating), blue flame (normal heating) and almost colourless, roaring flame (strong heating)

questions.q: How do you smell a substance safely?
questions.a: You waft a little of the smell towards your nose

questions.q: Give the reaction scheme for the rusting of iron, with state symbols
questions.a: iron (s) + water (l) + oxygen (g) → rust (s)
